RFC8950-3-2.note: The next hop is the VPN-IPv6 address with an 8-octet RD set to zero. TestParseMPReachNLRI_VPNWithIPv6NextHop decodes a zero-RD 24-byte next hop, and a decoder that skips the RD would pass whatever the RD holds. TestMPReachNLRI_RoundTrip_VPN encodes an IPv4 next hop (the RFC 4364 12-byte form, a neighbouring rule) and asserts only NH_Len = 12, never that the 8 RD bytes are zero. A writer emitting a non-zero RD passes both units. The 48-byte link-local form is untested.

RFC8950-4-1.note: MUST only advertise IPv4 or VPN-IPv4 NLRI with an IPv6 next hop after the peer advertised Extended Next Hop for the relevant AFI/SAFI pair. Both gaps of the earlier verdict are closed. (a) explicit next hop: Peer.resolveNextHop now refuses it without the pair; TestRFC8950ExplicitIPv6NextHopFollowsTheNegotiatedPair drives AnnounceNLRIBatch over a live pipe session with <1/1> only, <1/128> only and neither: IPv4 unicast is sent only with <1/1>, otherwise ErrNextHopIncompatible and no UPDATE on the wire; VPN-IPv4 resolves only with <1/128>. TestRFC8950BatchRailIPv4UnicastIPv6NextHopUsesMPReach shows the licensed route leaves as MP_REACH_NLRI 1/1 with the 16-octet next hop and the prefix, no NEXT_HOP and an empty NLRI field. (b) forward rails: TestRFC8950ForwardWithholdsIPv6NextHopFromPeerLackingThePair, general and route-server rails, received IPv6 next hop unchanged and explicit IPv6 next hop: the paired destination gets MP_REACH with that next hop, the unpaired one only the withdrawal half. Next-hop self stays proven by TestRFC8950IPv6NextHopFollowsTheNegotiatedPair. Observed-red records on canUseNextHopFor, inlineIPv4Unicast and egressNextHopLacksExtendedNextHop. Not asserted: the queued-drain path (same resolveNextHop producer) and VPN-IPv4 on the forward rails (same gate keyed by the MP_REACH family). Defect noted separately: both new gates apply to every AFI 1 family, beyond this rule's SAFIs.

RFC8950-4-2.note: MUST determine peer support through Capability Advertisement for the pair(s) of interest. TestNegotiateExtendedNextHop and ...Mismatch (capability/negotiated_test.go) prove both-advertise and remote-absent. An implementation that treated any remote ExtNH capability as support for every pair passes both tagged units. The untagged TestNegotiateExtendedNextHopMultipleFamilies tests per-tuple negotiation and would close the clause if tagged.

RFC8950-5-1.note: MUST NOT change the encoding of a next hop passed along unchanged. The non-compliant behaviour is the RR re-encoding the 16-byte IPv6 next hop. TestReactorForwardRRPreservesExtendedNextHop (reactor/forward_rr_test.go) asserts require.Equal(mpReach, attrs[14]) and the next-hop bytes 4:20, so any re-encoding goes red. Single-polarity positive per the row's marker.
